chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The prayer of the two Eids is two rak'ahs without a call (adhan) and without a proclamation (iqamah); there is nothing [specifically prescribed] before them or after them.

key_terms.صَلاَةُ اَلْعِيدَيْنِ: The prayer of the two Eids (Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha)

ai.seo_question: What is the number of rak'ahs and the call procedure for the Eid prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the procedural simplicity of the Eid prayer, distinguishing it from the five daily prayers by omitting the formal Adhan and Iqamah. The absence of specific Sunnah prayers immediately before or after underscores the Eid prayer's status as a standalone communal obligation (Wajib Kifai) rather than a voluntary addition to the daily routine. This ruling highlights the distinct juridical character of Eid as a celebration of divine favor, separate from the regular liturgical structure.
